relevant_sources.summary: The Dover 2024 Annual Report (10-K) provides evidence for the **governance** pillar of responsible AI. The report acknowledges risks associated with the "misuse of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies," indicating a need for oversight. Furthermore, it mentions investments in AI, a dedicated team focused on AI model development, and defined processes for synergy realization, all of which suggest a structured approach and commitment to managing AI initiatives.

summary.overall_findings: Dover's published materials address governance and privacy, with governance disclosures acknowledging risks associated with the misuse of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies. These are the only two responsible AI pillars with documented evidence out of 7 evaluated, with privacy policies outlining consumer rights concerning data processing and mentioning the potential for appeal of automated decisions. Based on a review of 6 publicly available sources, no qualifying public evidence was found for the majority of the 7 evaluated pillars.
